PAIN RELIEF DOESN'T HAVE TO BE A PILL.
THIS ISN'T DRUGSTORE CREAM. IT'S PRESCRIPTION MEDICINE.
Not menthol. Not tiger balm. Not a scented lotion pretending to be medicine.
This is 3% prescription Ketorolac, the formula the Boston Red Sox has used for years. Compounded to order, and strong enough to need a doctor's sign-off.
Why does that matter? Menthol distracts you from pain. A prescription NSAID reduces it — at the source. It doesn't mask the pain with a warming sensation. It reduces the inflammation causing it.

THE SCIENCE
THE TWO-LAYER RELIEF SYSTEM
Pain relief has two layers. Drugstore creams work on the first: your skin. KETRO RX works on the second: the inflamed tissue underneath.
Pills reach that second layer too, but only by flooding your entire system to get there. Ketorolac through the skin goes straight to the spot. Never through your gut, never through your liver, never anywhere it doesn't need to be.
01
LAYER 1: THE SURFACE
Where drugstore creams stop. Menthol and camphor tingle the skin, a sensation that distracts from pain without treating it.
02
LAYER 2: THE TISSUE
Where the pain actually lives. 3% prescription ketorolac absorbs through the skin into the inflamed tissue and reduces inflammation at the source.
